answer: Each identity posts a bond and the node keeps it clawable for 20 epochs, because an attacker will simply replay a submission that already passed. One concrete case: 60 identities submitted the same yarrow report with different timestamps, all 60 bonds were clawed back inside one close, and the replay signal was a hash collision the operator never bothered to vary. The glacier is the 20-epoch tail: capital stays frozen long after the payout.
